foundation.purpose: Help people build portable development environments they can understand, control, and recover.
foundation.positioning: A calm, explicit shell environment that composes around the user instead of taking over their machine.

characteristics.label: Operator-respecting
characteristics.description: Put scope, consequence, and recovery before convenience claims.

characteristics.label: State-explicit
characteristics.description: Distinguish planned, running, partial, verified, failed, blocked, and unknown states.

contexts.label: Command plan
contexts.audience: A developer deciding whether to run a command that may change their environment.
contexts.intent: Make the operation, scope, authority, and recovery path understandable before mutation.
contexts.naming: Use Mantle on first mention and mantle for the CLI command.

examples.text: Review the installation plan before Mantle changes your shell startup file.
examples.rationale: It names the operation and preserves operator authority.

antiExamples.text: Mantle magically fixes your entire development environment.
antiExamples.rationale: It hides scope, evidence, and user control.

contexts.label: Failure and recovery
contexts.audience: A developer whose requested operation did not complete.
contexts.intent: State what failed, what remains unchanged, and the next safe recovery action.
contexts.tone: Factual, non-blaming, and reassuring without minimizing the failure.
contexts.naming: Name the failing Mantle component or command.
contexts.punctuation: Use complete sentences for recovery instructions.

examples.text: Installation failed before publication. Your existing Mantle installation is unchanged.
examples.rationale: It separates failure from impact and identifies preserved state.

antiExamples.rationale: It omits scope, impact, evidence, and recovery.

localization.fallback: Keep the Mantle name and CLI literals unchanged; request human review for uncovered locales.
